incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: org=aerolite exceeded org-rate qps threshold (past 5m avg 9.8k, spike to 12.3k). Error rate rising 5% -> 12%. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: Got it — I'm on pager. Looking at dashboard now, correlating with model xfer latency and shard saturations.
liz-nguyen: Seeing lots of short-lived chat sessions — likely bot traffic. Customer support (maria-cs) notified?
maria-cs: Yep, reached out to Aerolite. They say a new campaign started ~08:05 UTC. They're pausing it after we confirm mitigation.
sam-ops: Can we do an emergency soft-throttle per-org first (avoid org-wide hard cut)? Suggest 60% of current RPS as temporary buffer.
oncall-sre: Agreed. Proposing: set org token-bucket to 600rps, burst 1200 (current observed ~1200 steady per shard). Will apply via admin CLI.
oncall-sre: Executing: 
```
# emergency fastpatch
adminctl org update-rate --org aerolite --rate 600 --burst 1200 --window 1s --reason "emergency spike - apply soft throttle"
```

incident-bot: :gear: adminctl task queued (task_id=task_7060001234_1) — will report status.
oncall-sre: Task completed OK. New enforcement active (600rps burst=1200). Observing metrics...
jordan-engineering: Observability shows p50 latency down 35%, errors dropping to 3.2%. Good. Any downstream retry storms?
oncall-sre: Not seeing retries spike beyond normal. Cache hit rate improved slightly due to reduced concurrency.
maria-cs: Aerolite confirms campaign paused on their side and sees fewer 429s. They're still concerned about degraded UX.
liz-nguyen: Propose also toggling a non-essential feature flag that amplifies requests (analytics ping) to reduce load while they recover. Can devs flip it quickly?
jordan-engineering: Can flip via feature-gate service. I'll coordinate a quick disable.
jordan-engineering: Running: `fgctl set aerolite analytics_pings --enabled false --tag incident-7060001234`
incident-bot: feature-gate: change accepted (fg_task=fg_8201).

sam-ops: Noting mitigation steps: (1) per-org soft throttle applied, (2) analytics pings disabled, (3) customer paused campaign. Recommend holding for 15m monitoring then gradual relax.
oncall-sre: Agreed. Setting follow-up check-in 10m.
(10 minutes later)
noncall-sre: 10m check — traffic stabilized at ~580rps, peak bursts ~1100, error rate 1.1%. CPU on serving pools back to normal.
maria-cs: Aerolite reports acceptable behavior and will resume campaign at reduced cadence tomorrow. They asked for a short summary email of actions — I'll send.
liz-nguyen: I'll capture the steps for the post-incident note. Quick list: adminctl change, feature-gate disable, customer pause.
jordan-engineering: Re-enabling analytics_pings now with gradual ramp: `fgctl set aerolite analytics_pings --enabled true --ramp 10m --tag incident-7060001234`
incident-bot: feature-gate: ramp scheduled (fg_task=fg_8202).
sam-ops: Plan for rollback: if traffic >900rps for 3 consecutive mins -> reapply 600rps throttle and notify oncall.
oncall-sre: I'll stay on for 30 more minutes to watch. Handoff after that to oncall rotation.
maria-cs: Sending customer summary now and confirming postmortem invite.
liz-nguyen: Thanks all — summarizing for incident log and assigning to eng for follow-up root cause (likely campaign bot behavior + missing client-side rate-smoothing).
oncall-sre: Closing immediate mitigation. Leaving note: mitigation_type=org_soft_throttle; rate=600; burst=1200; feature_gate=analytics_pings disabled; duration=~12m active.
incident-bot: Incident archived in incident tracker (id=INC-2026-7060).
